title: How to live stream a wedding with a drone: plan, gear and setup
description: Live stream a wedding with a DJI drone for guests who can’t be there: the plan, gear list, private YouTube link, phone or laptop setup, and the safety rules to follow.
h1: How to live stream a wedding with a drone
lead: To live stream a wedding with a drone, fly a DJI drone with RTMP, send DJI Fly’s picture to Stream My Drone on a phone or laptop, and broadcast it as an unlisted YouTube stream whose link you share with guests who cannot attend. Use the drone for the outdoor moments only (arrival, outdoor ceremony, group photo), keep it away from the guests, and let a second person run the stream.
summary: A drone adds the wide outdoor shots; it does not replace a ground camera for the vows, the speeches or anything indoors.
Two people work best: a pilot who only flies, and an operator who watches the stream and the chat.
An unlisted YouTube stream is the simplest private option: only people with the link can watch, and the recording stays on the channel afterwards.
Plan around 20–30 minutes of real flight per battery and bring at least three batteries, a power bank and a phone hotspot with 6–10 Mbps upload.
Ask the couple and the venue, follow your country’s drone rules and never fly over the guests.

sections.h2: Plan a wedding drone live stream in 6 steps

steps.d: Agree with the couple which moments go live, ask the venue whether drones are allowed, and check your country’s drone rules for the location.
The pilot flies and looks only at the drone. A second person runs Stream My Drone, watches the picture and answers the chat.
In YouTube Studio, create a stream with the visibility set to Unlisted and copy the stream URL and key into Stream My Drone. Send the link to guests a day before.

steps.t: Test the network at the venue
steps.d: Check mobile upload where you will stand. Turn on the operator’s phone hotspot, join the controller to it, and send a two-minute test stream.

steps.t: Go live for the key moments
steps.d: Start the stream a few minutes early and fly only for the planned shots. Between flights the stream can stay on with the drone landed.
After the event the unlisted stream becomes a video on the channel. The drone’s own recording is sharper and can be edited into the wedding film.

blocks.p: For most weddings the phone-only setup is enough for the outdoor part. The laptop setup adds what a drone cannot give: the vows in close-up with clean sound. The virtual camera guide shows how the drone appears in OBS.

sections.h2: Moments that work well from the air

list: The arrival of the couple and the guests’ cars, from a safe distance.
A slow reveal of the venue and the landscape before the ceremony starts.
The outdoor ceremony as a wide shot, high enough that the drone is not heard.
The group photo from above, with everyone looking up.
The couple’s walk or first dance outdoors at sunset.
Never fly over the guests. Keep a clear distance from people, trees and power lines.
Avoid flying indoors: without satellite positioning the drone drifts, and a hall is full of people.
Keep the drone high or landed during the vows; its sound carries.
Follow your country’s drone rules: registration, line of sight and permits for events.
Some guests do not want to appear online. Keep the link private and tell people the event is streamed.

blocks.p: The drone has no useful microphone; DJI Fly sends the controller’s microphone. In Stream My Drone on a phone, the operator can switch on the phone microphone to add commentary. For the vows and speeches, use the laptop setup with an external microphone or the venue’s sound system.

faq.q: Can you live stream a wedding with a drone?
faq.a: Yes. A DJI drone with RTMP in DJI Fly sends its picture to Stream My Drone on a phone or laptop, which broadcasts it to YouTube, Instagram or Facebook. Use it for the outdoor moments and a ground camera for the vows.

faq.q: How do guests who can’t attend watch privately?
faq.a: Create an unlisted YouTube stream and share its link. Only people with the link can watch, and the stream stays available as a video afterwards.

faq.q: Is it allowed to fly a drone at a wedding?
faq.a: It depends on your country’s drone rules and the venue. Ask the venue, follow local registration and permit rules, and never fly over people.

faq.q: How long can a drone stream a wedding?
faq.a: One battery gives about 20–30 minutes of real flight. Bring three or more and fly only for the planned moments; the stream itself can keep running between flights.

faq.q: Do I need a laptop to stream a wedding with a drone?
faq.a: No. With a DJI RC 2, a phone running Stream My Drone is enough. A laptop with OBS helps when you want to mix the drone with ground cameras and ceremony sound.

faq.q: What internet do I need at the venue?
faq.a: About 6–10 Mbps of steady upload for each platform. A 4G or 5G phone hotspot usually works; test it at the venue beforehand.
